subject.title: Gateway runtime: "no such table: plugin_state_entries / acp_sessions" despite tables existing in state/openclaw.sqlite (agent turns produce no reply)

question: Should maintainers start a fix from the paired missing-table errors now, or first require redacted runtime diagnostics proving which SQLite database the failing Docker gateway process is opening?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but the reported contradiction depends on live path resolution; choosing a fix without the runtime pathname could add the wrong compatibility or recovery behavior.

options.title: Collect runtime path proof first
options.body: Ask for redacted `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, resolved shared DB path, `PRAGMA database_list`, and the exact `openclaw.sqlite` path seen by the failing gateway process before selecting a fix boundary.

options.title: Build a Docker repro branch
options.body: Use the report as enough signal to create a Docker regression covering gateway run, device-pair notify polling, `chat.history`, and `sessions.send` with the stated environment.

options.title: Fold into shared-state DB ownership work
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader shared SQLite ownership/recovery cluster only if maintainers decide the missing-table errors are another symptom of that policy work.

recommendation.title: Collect runtime path proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, resolved shared DB path, `PRAGMA database_list`, and the exact `openclaw.sqlite` path seen by the failing gateway process before selecting a fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is the shared SQLite state DB and ACP metadata persistence history on the affected tables.
